context.body: Selected for the reader trail because “The kind of death signaled by being lifted up” preserves a distinct antecedent source unit within anticipation.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Troubled speech about the hour leads to prayer, a heavenly voice, crowd questions, and a final summons to walk in the light.
observations.label: The kind of death signaled by being lifted up: textual observation

observations.body: “Lifted up” is spoken publicly and then interpreted by the narrator as indicating the kind of death Jesus would die.
observations.label: The kind of death signaled by being lifted up: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Jesus, the Father’s voice, the crowd, and the narrator each contribute a distinct statement.
observations.label: Relationships named in John 12:27–36

payload.posture: Read John 12:27–36 as its own anticipation and stated approach crucifixion setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The crowd recognizes death language in the saying but cannot reconcile it with what it has heard about the Christ.
payload.title: The kind of death signaled by being lifted up
